paragraphs: Graph neural networks can lose knowledge of earlier tasks as they learn new ones. Replaying stored examples helps, but graph examples depend on their connections as well as their individual features. If a replay buffer fails to preserve those relationships, the stored inputs may no longer support their associated labels correctly.

TACO keeps past information in a smaller graph. During each learning period, it joins this stored graph with the incoming graph and aligns nodes shared between them. It then reduces the combined graph again to keep its size stable. The reduction uses proximity between node representations to preserve essential graph structure while shrinking the memory.

The experiments show that learning on the reduced graph can closely approximate learning on the original graph. Comparisons with a broad collection of existing methods also favor TACO. These findings support preserving the quality of connections in replay memory: a compact graph can retain useful learning context that a collection of disconnected examples would miss.
neurips-2024-a-topology-aware-graph-coar.tldr: TACO reduces forgetting in continual graph learning by maintaining a compact replay graph that preserves important connections.

paragraphs: Mutual information measures statistical dependence between variables, but estimating it becomes difficult as their number of dimensions grows. The sample requirements can become impractical even when the dependence itself has a simpler structure. This paper investigates whether learned representations can expose that structure and make estimation feasible.

The proposed latent mutual information approximation, LMI, first learns low-dimensional representations through a simple architecture motivated by theory. It then applies a nonparametric mutual information estimator to those representations. In benchmarks, LMI approximates mutual information well for variables with more than a thousand dimensions when their dependence is captured by the low-dimensional representations. That condition is central to the result.

The authors also apply LMI to two biological questions. Their analysis finds that protein language model representations contain nontrivial information about protein interactions. In measurements of blood-forming stem cells, they identify a sharp rise in information about cell fate during neutrophil differentiation. These examples show how the approximation can reveal dependencies in complex biological measurements.
neurips-2024-approximating-mutual-inform.tldr: LMI estimates dependence in high-dimensional data through learned compact representations when those representations capture the dependence structure.

paragraphs: A conventional regression model uses one set of parameters for all samples. Individualized regression allows those parameters to vary between samples, making it relevant when a shared model cannot adequately describe individual differences. This paper develops that idea for matrix-valued data, motivated by medical imaging and personalized medicine.

The proposed framework derives individualization from an optimized map of relationships within the samples themselves. It does not require additional information specifying how similar different samples are for the individualized coefficients. This makes the internal structure of the supplied data the basis for adapting the model, rather than requiring a separate source of sample relationships.

The authors call the method Attention boosted Individualized Regression because its relationship map is closely connected to self-attention. That connection also offers an interpretation of attention as a way to construct individualized models. Numerical experiments and an analysis of brain MRI data from ADNI report superior performance, providing evidence for the framework in both experimental and medical-imaging settings.
neurips-2024-attention-boosted-individua.tldr: Attention boosted Individualized Regression learns sample-specific models for matrix data using internal relationships without additional sample-similarity information.

paragraphs: Building operations affect occupant comfort, health, and safety, while buildings account for roughly one-third of global energy use. Improving their performance therefore has both human and environmental value. Research toward that goal has been constrained by limited access to comprehensive real-world data covering multiple aspects of building operation.

The Building TimeSeries dataset addresses this gap with observations from three buildings over three years. The authors describe more than ten thousand timeseries data points and hundreds of unique ontologies. Metadata follows the Brick schema, giving the data a standardized descriptive structure. This matters for interoperability: building analytics must work with the meanings of measurements as well as their numerical values.

The paper demonstrates the dataset through benchmarks for timeseries ontology classification and zero-shot forecasting. These examine identifying the kinds of recorded series and forecasting in a zero-shot setting. The authors position the benchmarks as an initial step toward resolving interoperability challenges, with the dataset and benchmarking code available to support further building analytics research.
neurips-2024-building-timeseries-dataset.tldr: BTS provides three years of operational data from three buildings, standardized metadata, and benchmarks for classification and zero-shot forecasting.

paragraphs: Adversarial camouflage aims to make vehicles harder for automated detectors to recognize. Previous work emphasizes attack effectiveness and robustness, but optimizing vehicle textures pixel by pixel can create conspicuous patterns. A camouflage pattern may therefore confuse a detector while remaining easy for a person to notice as unusual.

CNCA addresses visual appearance and customization using an existing pretrained diffusion model. A user supplies a text prompt, and the method samples a texture image from the model while seeking strong adversarial performance. The generative model provides a way to search for textures that reflect the requested appearance, bringing user control into the camouflage-generation process.

The authors evaluate the method in digital and physical experiments and through user studies. They report substantially more natural-looking camouflage than leading comparison methods, together with competitive attack performance. The contribution is an empirical improvement in the balance between appearance and detector interference. The reported result supports combining those objectives without claiming that the method exceeds existing attacks on every measure.
neurips-2024-cnca-toward-customizable-an.tldr: CNCA uses a pretrained diffusion model and text prompts to produce more natural-looking vehicle camouflage with competitive adversarial effectiveness.

paragraphs: Federated learning trains models collaboratively while keeping data with local clients, but this paper identifies a privacy vulnerability when the trained models are diffusion models. The authors show that multiple backdoors can control generation through different triggers, enabling an attacker to recover substantial amounts of private client data.

Their Combinatorial Triggers approach demonstrates this DataStealing task in a basic federated learning system. Distance-based defenses can still filter its malicious updates by comparing them with other client updates. The authors therefore introduce AdaSCP, which uses gradient information from influential diffusion timesteps to assess parameter importance and adapt the scale of selected updates.

This adaptation makes the malicious update resemble benign updates under the distance comparisons used by those defenses. Experiments demonstrate leakage involving thousands of training images and show AdaSCP defeating advanced distance-based defenses in the evaluated settings. The findings expose a gap between keeping training data locally managed and preventing a collaboratively trained generator from revealing that data through manipulated behavior.
neurips-2024-datastealing-steal-data-fro.tldr: DataStealing demonstrates that backdoored federated diffusion models can leak thousands of private images, including under evaluated distance-based defenses.

paragraphs: Variational inference approximates a difficult probability distribution with a more manageable one. EigenVI constructs these approximations using orthogonal function expansions. For real-valued variables, the lowest-order approximation is Gaussian, while additional terms systematically introduce non-Gaussian structure. This allows the approximation to describe asymmetry and multiple modes while retaining accessible sampling and low-order moments.

EigenVI chooses an approximation by matching the target distribution's score function, which describes how its log density changes. It minimizes a stochastic estimate of Fisher divergence, a measure of score mismatch. The resulting optimization becomes a minimum eigenvalue problem, avoiding the iterative gradient-based optimization used by many black-box variational inference methods and its associated tuning choices.

Different families of orthogonal functions also let the approach handle nonnegative or bounded variables. The authors test EigenVI on varied target distributions, including Bayesian models from posteriordb, and find higher accuracy than existing Gaussian black-box variational inference methods on those targets. The results support combining a flexible approximation family with a different computational route to fitting it.
neurips-2024-eigenvi-score-based-variati.tldr: EigenVI fits flexible probability approximations through score matching that reduces to a minimum eigenvalue problem.

paragraphs: This paper studies a promised version of distribution identity testing. One discrete distribution is available through samples, and another is fully specified. Both have support size k. The tester must distinguish exact equality from a difference of at least epsilon in Shannon entropy, with high probability. The promise excludes unequal distributions whose entropies are too close.

The authors establish a nearly optimal sample requirement of square root of k divided by epsilon, plus one divided by epsilon squared, ignoring logarithmic factors. Near optimality means the sample bound is close to the fundamental requirement for this particular testing problem. It concerns the stated equality-or-entropy-gap distinction, rather than unrestricted testing of every possible difference between distributions.

They then apply the result to identity testing for Bayesian networks with n dimensions and maximum in-degree d. The new upper bound improves the earlier sample complexity dependence and removes an additional structural assumption required by the previous result. This connects a guarantee about entropy testing to more efficient testing of distributions represented by structured networks.
neurips-2024-entropy-testing-and-its-app.tldr: The paper gives near-optimal sample bounds for promised entropy identity testing and improves identity-testing bounds for Bayesian networks.

paragraphs: Removing an unwanted concept from a text-to-image diffusion model can also damage its ability to generate unrelated content. Existing approaches try to control this interference by preserving neutral content or restricting changes to model parameters. The paper focuses on the unresolved trade-off between effective removal and preservation of the model's remaining capabilities.

The proposed method identifies concepts that are most affected by parameter changes and explicitly works to preserve them. The authors call these vulnerable concepts adversarial concepts. This directs preservation toward the content most exposed to damage during editing, rather than relying only on a general preference for small parameter changes or on preserving neutral examples.

Experiments with Stable Diffusion show the method outperforming leading concept-erasure approaches in removing unwanted content while maintaining unrelated elements. The findings support the idea that identifying what is most vulnerable to an edit can improve the edit itself. Here, preservation is an active part of learning how to erase a target concept with minimal effects on other concepts.
neurips-2024-erasing-undesirable-concept.tldr: The method improves diffusion-model concept erasure by identifying and protecting unrelated concepts most vulnerable to parameter changes.

paragraphs: Federated models can encounter several kinds of unfamiliar data simultaneously. Covariate shifts call for generalization across changed input distributions, while semantic shifts call for detecting unfamiliar content. The paper argues that addressing these separately leaves a gap when both occur in deployment, alongside data that matches the training distribution.

FOOGD estimates each client's probability density and uses a global distribution to guide subsequent federated learning. Its SM3D component estimates a score model for arbitrary distributions without prior constraints and uses score values to detect semantic shifts. Its SAG component supplies knowledge intended to be both invariant and diverse, supporting generalization within clients and across client performance.

Empirical evaluations report three benefits: reliable estimation of decentralized, non-normalized distributions; detection of semantic shifts through score values; and better covariate-shift generalization through feature-extractor regularization. The approach brings detection and generalization into one framework. Its stated findings suggest that distribution information shared through federated collaboration can help models both recognize unfamiliar data and handle changes they should generalize across.
neurips-2024-foogd-federated-collaborati.tldr: FOOGD combines distribution estimation, semantic-shift detection, and covariate-shift generalization within federated learning.

paragraphs: Remote sensing can describe the physical cover of an urban landscape, but understanding how people use that landscape requires finer semantic information. The authors introduce FUSU to support mapping land use and its changes over time. They present it as the first fine-grained land use change segmentation dataset for urban semantic understanding.

FUSU contains 17 land use classes and 30 billion annotated pixels across 847 square kilometers in five geographically varied urban areas in northern and southern China. It combines high-resolution satellite images from two times, with ground sample distances of 0.2–0.5 meters, and monthly optical and radar satellite sequences. These sources bring detailed spatial observations together with repeated temporal measurements.

The paper also introduces a unified time-series architecture for change detection and segmentation, and benchmarks multiple methods across several tasks. The dataset provides a basis for developing models that connect urban image changes with categories of human activity. Its contribution is both the annotated resource and an initial framework for evaluating methods that use its spatial and temporal information.
neurips-2024-fusu-a-multi-temporal-sourc.tldr: FUSU combines detailed land use annotations with high-resolution and monthly satellite imagery to study urban land use changes.

paragraphs: G-Retriever lets users ask conversational questions about graphs whose elements carry text. It produces written answers and highlights relevant graph portions. The work targets real-world textual graphs across applications such as scene understanding, common sense reasoning, and knowledge graph reasoning, extending beyond standard graph classification tasks or simple queries on small graphs.

The authors introduce a GraphQA benchmark assembled from different tasks and a retrieval-augmented generation framework for answering its questions. G-Retriever selects graph material through a Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree optimization problem. This provides a structured way to retrieve relevant graph content for the language model, including when the full graph exceeds the model's context window. Soft prompting supports fine-tuning for graph understanding.

Evaluations across multiple domains show stronger performance than the compared baselines, good scaling to larger graphs, and reduced hallucination. These findings support retrieving a relevant graph portion as a practical connection between graph data and language generation. Highlighting that portion also exposes which graph material accompanies the answer, making the response more directly tied to the underlying graph.
neurips-2024-g-retriever-retrieval-augme.tldr: G-Retriever answers questions about textual graphs by retrieving relevant graph portions, improving evaluated performance and reducing hallucination.

paragraphs: Causal discovery seeks the directed graph underlying relationships among observed variables. Approaches based on functional causal models can identify a unique graph, but they may struggle with high dimensionality or require strong parametric assumptions. This paper proposes recovering the global structure by making use of smaller, local causal relationships.

The first stage builds a compact hierarchy from ancestral relationships in linear structural causal models. This hierarchy captures more causal information than a single linear ordering. The authors show that the approach extends to nonlinear settings with arbitrary noise. A second, nonparametric stage removes spurious edges by searching for local conditioning sets, using local evidence to refine the overall graph.

The paper provides correctness guarantees and worst-case polynomial time bounds for its algorithms, along with experiments on synthetic data. It reports greater accuracy than current methods for the edge-pruning approach. The contribution combines a richer representation of causal ordering with local search, linking global organization and local constraints in a framework for linear and nonlinear additive noise models.
neurips-2024-hybrid-top-down-global-caus.tldr: The method combines hierarchical causal ordering with local edge pruning, supported by correctness guarantees and synthetic-data evaluations.

paragraphs: Continual learning must acquire new knowledge while retaining what a model learned earlier. This often creates a trade-off between old-task retention and new-task performance. The paper reframes both difficulties in terms of sensitivity to parameter updates: excessive sensitivity can cause previous predictions to change sharply and can also encourage overfitting to new tasks.

The proposed learning approach optimizes performance against a parameter distribution that produces the worst continual-learning performance within a neighborhood of distributions. This makes sensitivity to nearby parameter changes part of the training objective. Reducing that sensitivity is intended to stabilize older predictions while also preventing the model from fitting new tasks too narrowly.

The authors report simultaneous improvements in knowledge retention and new-task performance, with both theoretical and empirical support. They also describe the approach as compatible with existing continual-learning methods and report improvements in effectiveness, efficiency, and versatility. Its main contribution is a shared optimization perspective on two problems often treated as competing objectives, allowing sensitivity control to complement established continual-learning techniques.
neurips-2024-model-sensitivity-aware-con.tldr: The method controls sensitivity to parameter updates to improve both retention of old tasks and performance on new ones.

paragraphs: Fragment-based molecule generation builds candidates from smaller molecular pieces. Many existing methods mostly rearrange or slightly modify the fragments already in a database, restricting exploration. The proposed f-RAG framework uses retrieval alongside a pretrained molecular generator to retain useful known fragments while generating additional ones.

The method retrieves two kinds of fragments with different roles. Hard fragments must appear as building blocks in the resulting molecule. Soft fragments act as references that guide new-fragment generation through a trainable injection module. This separation gives retrieved information both a direct structural role and an indirect guiding role, allowing the generator to go beyond the pieces it explicitly preserves.

An iterative refinement process adds generated fragments back into the vocabulary, and subsequent genetic fragment modification further supports exploration. The fragment pool can therefore evolve instead of remaining fixed throughout generation. The authors state that this process can improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off by combining a strong generative prior with a growing collection of novel, high-quality fragments.
neurips-2024-molecule-generation-with-fr.tldr: f-RAG combines required and guiding molecular fragments with generation and iterative vocabulary expansion to explore beyond an initial fragment database.

paragraphs: Detecting indoor objects in three dimensions from multiple images depends on recovering accurate geometry. The paper identifies inaccurate geometry from an earlier NeRF-based approach as a source of weaker detection. MVSDet instead uses plane sweeps to make image features useful for geometry-aware three-dimensional object detection.

Accurate depth prediction can require many candidate depth planes, so MVSDet introduces probabilistic sampling and soft weighting to control that cost. For each pixel, it chooses several locations with high scores in a probability volume. Those scores express confidence and determine how the pixel's features contribute to the three-dimensional volume, retaining multiple promising placements rather than depending on only one.

The method also uses pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting to regularize depth prediction, improving detection with little additional computation. Experiments on ScanNet and ARKitScenes demonstrate the model's superiority in the reported comparisons. The approach connects depth uncertainty directly to feature placement, making geometry estimation part of the detection process while reducing the need for a large collection of depth planes.
neurips-2024-mvsdet-multi-view-indoor-3d.tldr: MVSDet improves multi-view indoor 3D detection using probabilistic plane sweeps and Gaussian Splatting to guide geometry estimation.

paragraphs: Distributional reinforcement learning approximates the distribution of returns, describing the range of possible outcomes rather than only their average. This paper introduces a model-based algorithm for that problem and analyzes it in the generative model regime. Its central contribution is a guarantee about how efficiently return distributions can be approximated in that setting.

The authors prove minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors. This means the algorithm's requirement is close to the best achievable worst-case requirement under the analyzed regime. They identify this as the first guarantee of its kind for a distributional reinforcement learning algorithm. The scope of the result is the generative model setting specified in the paper.

The analysis also offers theoretical perspectives on categorical distributional methods and introduces a stochastic categorical cumulative-distribution-function Bellman equation. The authors expect this equation to be useful independently of the algorithm. An experimental comparison of several model-based distributional approaches complements the theory and provides practical takeaways, connecting a worst-case guarantee with an empirical study of algorithm choices.
neurips-2024-near-minimax-optimal-distri.tldr: A new model-based distributional RL algorithm achieves minimax-optimal return-distribution approximation up to logarithmic factors in the generative model regime.

paragraphs: Independent component analysis seeks to recover underlying sources from mixed signals with limited knowledge of the sources or mixing process. Many estimation algorithms exist, but their weaknesses differ. This paper develops a diagnostic score for choosing among ICA solutions when the observations contain arbitrary Gaussian noise.

The score evaluates an estimated mixing matrix using the data's characteristic function. It requires a finite second moment but does not require knowing the noise distribution's parameters. This provides a nonparametric way to assess candidate solutions in the noisy setting, making algorithm selection responsive to the observed data rather than assuming one estimator is appropriate throughout.

The authors also introduce contrast functions and algorithms with fast computability comparable to FASTICA and JADE, including applicability in domains where those methods may fail. They acknowledge that the new algorithms can have weaknesses too, and simulations show how the diagnostic can help remedy them through selection. A theoretical framework analyzes local and global convergence, complementing the practical contribution of evaluating alternative solutions.
neurips-2024-nonparametric-evaluation-of.tldr: A nonparametric diagnostic selects among noisy ICA solutions using finite-second-moment data without knowing Gaussian noise parameters.

paragraphs: Implicit neural video coding trains a network to fit a particular video and stores compressed network parameters as the video's representation. The paper argues that simple parameter-compression methods partly explain why earlier approaches trail leading standard codecs. NVRC therefore concentrates on compressing the learned representation rather than primarily redesigning its architecture.

The framework introduces quantization and entropy coding that allow end-to-end optimization of the rate-distortion trade-off: balancing bitrate against reconstruction error. It also hierarchically compresses the network, quantization, and entropy-model parameters. Accounting for all of these components matters because the models used to compress a representation introduce storage overhead of their own.

Experiments show NVRC outperforming many conventional and learned benchmark codecs. On the UVG dataset, the authors report a 23% average coding gain over VVC VTM in Random Access mode, measured using PSNR. They describe this level of performance as a first for an implicit-neural-representation codec to their knowledge. The result demonstrates the importance of optimizing the complete compressed representation.
neurips-2024-nvrc-neural-video-represent.tldr: NVRC jointly optimizes neural video representation compression, reporting a 23% average coding gain over VVC VTM Random Access on UVG.

paragraphs: An agent may receive complex, high-dimensional observations even when the underlying environment evolves according to relatively simple hidden dynamics. This paper asks when reinforcement learning remains statistically tractable in that situation and when algorithms for the hidden system can be adapted to observable inputs.

The statistical results include a negative finding: most well-studied function-approximation settings become intractable when combined with rich observations. Simple latent dynamics alone therefore do not establish tractability in those settings. The authors also identify latent pushforward coverability as a general condition that enables statistical tractability, providing a positive counterpart to the difficulty result.

On the algorithmic side, the paper gives provably efficient reductions that turn an arbitrary algorithm for the latent decision process into one that works with rich observations. These reductions apply in two settings: access to hindsight observations of latent dynamics, or the ability to estimate self-predictive latent models. Together, the results clarify both an obstacle and specific routes toward separating representation issues from learning the underlying dynamics.
neurips-2024-reinforcement-learning-unde.tldr: The paper identifies tractability barriers and sufficient conditions for latent-dynamics RL, plus efficient reductions in two specified settings.

paragraphs: A visual question may be impossible to answer from the image currently available. Humans can recognize this and seek another view, whereas vision-language models commonly produce a direct response. This paper studies whether a model can instead explain how to adjust an image so that the missing visual information becomes available.

The task connects assessing information sufficiency with guiding information acquisition. The authors introduce a human-labeled dataset to evaluate this capability and an automated framework that creates synthetic training examples by simulating situations where more visual information is needed. They identify assistance for visually impaired people capturing images as a particularly valuable application of this guidance.

Fine-tuning mainstream vision-language models with the synthetic examples produces significant performance improvements in the reported experiments. This suggests that training on information-seeking situations can strengthen a capability that direct question answering does not adequately exercise. The findings show potential to bring models closer to human behavior in assessing and acquiring information, without establishing that the broader human-model gap has been closed.
neurips-2024-right-this-way-can-vlms-gui.tldr: A new benchmark and synthetic training framework improve VLMs' ability to guide image adjustments when a question needs more visual information.

paragraphs: Backdoor scanning aims to identify models whose behavior has been maliciously altered. Existing scanners can depend on assumptions about the attack, and the authors observe difficulties with classifiers whose backdoors were introduced using adversarial training. TRODO searches for a behavioral signature that does not require knowing the backdoor method or its label mapping.

The signature concerns blind spots where a trojaned classifier treats out-of-distribution samples as in-distribution. TRODO probes these regions by adversarially shifting unfamiliar samples toward the model's in-distribution behavior. An increased likelihood that the perturbed samples are accepted as in-distribution serves as evidence for detecting a trojan, connecting the scan to how the model responds outside familiar data.

The authors report high accuracy and adaptability across multiple datasets and scenarios, including adversarially trained trojaned classifiers. The approach can also operate without the original training data. These findings support its potential as a broadly applicable scanner under the evaluated conditions, with the central benefit being reduced reliance on prior knowledge about how an attack was constructed.
neurips-2024-scanning-trojaned-models-us.tldr: TRODO detects backdoored classifiers by probing whether perturbed out-of-distribution samples are unusually likely to be treated as in-distribution.

paragraphs: Learning rate and batch size strongly influence optimizer behavior, so changing one raises the question of how to adjust the other. Scaling rules developed for SGD-style methods often increase the learning rate with batch size. This paper investigates why that relationship does not carry over directly to Adam-style optimizers.

The theoretical analysis focuses on updates based on the sign of the gradient. In this setting, the authors prove that the optimal learning rate initially increases as batch size grows, reaches a peak, and then decreases. They also show that the peak moves toward larger batch sizes as training progresses. The resulting relationship is a surge rather than a continuously increasing scaling rule.

Experiments across computer vision and natural language processing tasks support the proposed law. These findings make training stage relevant to the learning-rate and batch-size relationship, alongside optimizer type. The result motivates tuning that accounts for the rise and fall, while preserving the distinction between the proof for sign-based updates and empirical evidence across the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2024-surge-phenomenon-in-optimal.tldr: For sign-based updates, the optimal learning rate rises then falls with batch size, with the peak shifting as training progresses.

paragraphs: The iNaturalist Sounds Dataset gathers 230,000 audio recordings covering more than 5,500 species, contributed by over 27,000 recordists worldwide. It includes birds, mammals, insects, reptiles, and amphibians. Both the audio and species labels come from observations submitted to the iNaturalist citizen science platform.

Recordings differ in length, and each has a single species annotation. The resulting labels are weak, so the dataset's usefulness cannot be judged solely by the amount of audio it contains. The authors benchmark multiple model backbones and compare multiclass training objectives with multilabel objectives, examining different ways to learn from this annotation structure.

Evaluations on strongly labeled downstream datasets show that iNatSounds is useful for pretraining despite its weak labels. Its freely accessible single archive also makes the collection available for broader research. The authors envision applications in public engagement and in helping biologists, ecologists, and land managers process large audio collections. Those uses are presented as future possibilities, while the demonstrated finding concerns its value as a pretraining resource.
neurips-2024-the-inaturalist-sounds-data.tldr: iNatSounds provides 230,000 wildlife recordings and demonstrates useful audio-model pretraining despite having only one species annotation per recording.

paragraphs: Sequential prediction assumes that earlier observations contain useful information about how later observations develop. Yet deciding whether a dataset has a meaningful evolving pattern often depends on expert judgment. This paper introduces a quantitative approach intended to help assess that structure and inform the use of sequential models.

Evolving Rate, or EvoRate, uses mutual information to approximate the intensity of evolving patterns. Such a measure can inform choices about temporal ordering and feature or data selection, in addition to model suitability. A practical complication arises when data consists of snapshots at different times without correspondence between observations, making direct estimation difficult.

To address missing correspondence, the authors introduce EvoRate_W, which uses optimal transport to establish correspondence for estimating first-order EvoRate. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, including images and tabular data, support the measure's effectiveness. The contribution combines a proposed numerical description of temporal structure with an estimation approach for snapshots that do not already provide the links needed to follow observations over time.
neurips-2024-towards-understanding-evolv.tldr: EvoRate uses mutual information to quantify evolving patterns, with an optimal-transport variant for temporal snapshots lacking correspondence.
